facts.fact: UNDP Cameroon says the software system now lets over 50,000 digital civil status documents be produced across 26 centres, after a Japan-funded initiative from 2020 equipped the centres of Gazawa, Kaele, Maroua 1, Maroua 2, Mokolo, Tokombere and Touloum; no total of centres is given and the figure is undated, so the date is the publication date.

UNDP Cameroon says that around Maroua 3 council seven secondary centres are now covered, five of them in hospitals, bringing registration to families at the moment of birth; at Dougoui about seven registrations are completed a week; date is the publication date.

At Maroua 3 council 343 certificates were issued for births, marriages and deaths from January to March, the year not stated, with birth certificates produced on the system while the parent waits, per UNDP Cameroon; date is the publication date.

Under the Denmark-funded Legal Identity and Social Cohesion Project of 2024-2025, UNDP and BUNEC are expanding digitalisation to ten more centres, five of them in the Far North (Koza, Meri, Mindif, Maroua 3, Mora), with updated software, backup power and training.

The digitalisation runs as a partnership between UNDP and BUNEC; the Maroua 3 council says BUNEC gives technical assistance on call and asks for a permanent on-site technician; date is the publication date.

The equipment installed from 2020 was funded by Japan under a legal identity initiative, and the 2024-2025 expansion to ten more centres by the Government of Denmark, UNDP and BUNEC, per UNDP Cameroon; the Maroua 3 mayor provides the internet connection.
